premises.text: Urban parking is painful and drives large amounts of circling traffic
premises.evidence_span: half of the traffic in Brooklyn is actually caused by people circling for a parking spot

premises.text: Curb Karma is a smartphone social network where leavers publish spots and seekers reserve them with map pinpointing, messaging, GPS navigation, and ratings
premises.evidence_span: you can participate in a social network for parking

premises.text: Karma Credits priced at $1 mediate reservations: seekers spend two credits, spot-givers earn one, and Curb Karma keeps one
premises.evidence_span: A Karma Credit is worth $1 and available for purchase in the App Store

premises.text: High-demand urban parking spots turn over enough that capturing a small share of exchanges yields meaningful city-level revenue, expandable globally
premises.evidence_span: only about 50,000 of those are considered in high demand

value.text: Find and reserve parking where and when you need it so everyone wins—seeker parks, leaver earns credit, platform earns
value.evidence_span: Curb Karma finds you parking where and when you need it

causal_links.evidence_span: Marissa can find and reserve Heather's parking spot
parking's actually a problem all over the world

notes: Publish/reserve/map/message/GPS/finish/rate demo cascade folded into one social parking app premise (§4.1.7). Credit split economics kept as separately revisable commercial mechanism. SF exchange math and IBM pain-index expansion folded into market premise. Free credit promo excluded.
